title: What Is Actually Clogging Your Kitchen Sink?
description: Slow-draining sinks are usually caused by materials trapped directly in the P-trap beneath your basin. In kitchen sinks, cooking fats, oils, and fine food debris cling to the interior pipe walls, solidifying into dense blockages over time. In bathroom drains, soap scum and hair bind together to form stubborn plugs. Avoid harsh chemical drain openers, which can generate extreme heat that damages PVC joints and corrodes rubber seals. Cleaning your P-trap manually into a bucket or using a simple drain tool is safer for your system. If water continues backing up, consult a qualified plumber to inspect the main branch line.
